description: Report what TronRelic's tracked energy rental markets did, as recorded on chain by each market's examiner: TRX paid by renters, energy delivered, the blended price paid in SUN per energy per day, how many sampled payments were served or never served, how fast deliveries followed payments, and how concentrated the suppliers are, plus one row of totals per UTC day. Use it first for any question about volume, revenue, prices paid, or which markets are busy or have gone quiet, over a day or a few weeks. Do not use it to check individual rentals (use resource-markets-list-rentals), for how a market is set up (use resource-markets-get-config), or for what a market advertises, its rate card, or what it pays holders (use resource-markets-get-prices; this tool reports prices renters actually paid). Read-only. Parameters: "slug" (optional), a market slug such as "catfee" or "tron-max-io", to report one market in full; "days" (optional), how many UTC days of daily totals to return, ending today, default 7, up to 14 for every market or 30 for one. Without "slug", returns { success, asOf, days, pageUrl, markets: [{ slug, displayName, pageUrl, observed, summary, daily }] }. The top-level "pageUrl" is TronRelic's page comparing every market, and each market's "pageUrl" is its TronRelic page with these figures; when you cite a figure, link the matching page so the reader can check it there. Either is null when the site address is unknown. "summary" is null for a market with no rental figures, and otherwise { windowDays, firstObservedAt, lastObservedAt, paymentTRX, energyDelivered, blendedSunPerEnergyPerDay, blendedPriceDay, sampledRentals, sampledServed, sampledDeliveryUnobserved, sampledUnserved, sampleCapped, medianFulfillmentMs, participantCount, topParticipantShare }; sampledRentals is sampledServed + sampledDeliveryUnobserved + sampledUnserved, and only the last is payments not answered: a delivery unobserved rental (0 for every market but trxFee) was paid for with no delivery to the payer seen and no sign the payer needed it, most likely an order for another wallet, so do not report it as a failure. "paymentTRX" and "energyDelivered" in the summary cover the whole "windowDays" and are exact. The "sampled" counts and the other per-rental figures come from at most the newest 5000 rentals in that window; "sampleCapped" true means the sample did not reach back through the whole window, so those counts are not totals. "lastObservedAt" is the chain time of the newest rental activity recorded; a time hours before "asOf" on a normally busy market means it has gone quiet or its examiner has stopped. "daily" is [{ day (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC), paymentTRX, energyDelivered, sunPerEnergyPerDay, rentalCount, deliveredRentalCount, deliveryUnobservedRentalCount }], oldest first, with no row for a day nothing was recorded. "rentalCount" is every rental that started that day, delivered or not, exact and not sampled; "deliveredRentalCount" is how many of those have a delivery; "deliveryUnobservedRentalCount" is how many were paid for but had a delivery the examiner could not observe, such as a trxFee order for another receiver whose payer showed no need of the energy (0 for every other market, and read as 0 when absent). rentalCount minus both is the rentals paid for but not (yet) delivered; resource-markets-get-errata lists them. All three leave out records a market's own figures treat as internal, such as CatFee paying itself or SoHu's collector loans, and all three are absent from a row when the count could not be taken. For SoHu and Tronex a rental is a delivery, so the two counts are equal. EnergyFather's summary and "daily" rows cover only the deliveries paid in TRX at its payment address, a small share of its sales; its API buyers pay from prepaid balances the chain does not show, so read its full delivery figures from "reports" with its slug. Today's row is partial, covering only up to the last time the figures were stored, normally less than an hour ago. "paymentTRX" counts what the examiner recorded as renter payments; how a market records prepaid-balance top-ups or unserved payments differs by market, so compare a market's days with each other rather than one market's TRX with another's. With "slug", returns { success, asOf, days, pageUrl, market } with the same fields plus "priceBuckets" (the price paid by rental length: bucket, label, rentalCount, median, min and max SUN per energy per day), "p90FulfillmentMs", "usdtTransferEnergy" (energy one USDT transfer costs, to convert SUN per energy into TRX per transfer), "reports" (figures from other analyses of the market), "advertisedPrice" (the cheapest and dearest advertised price per USDT transfer at the newest capture, or null), and "completeBefore" (the repair watermark). An unknown slug returns { success: false, error } listing the known slugs.

inputSchema.description: Which market to report, and how many days of daily totals.

days.description: UTC days of daily totals, ending today. Omit for 7. Up to 14 for every market, 30 for one.

slug.description: Market slug such as "catfee". Omit to report every market.

name: resource-markets-get-activity
title: Show energy market activity
